title: Felix and the Sigil Revisited
premise: Ansel Nystrom, a mercenary bound by oath to a god that fell silent a century ago, keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things—bottled grief, borrowed years, names that were never spoken. When the dying courier Felix presses a bloodstained map into her hands, Ansel discovers the sigil it bears is the same one seared into her own skin at her swearing-in: the mark of the silent god, who did not die but was imprisoned by the Guild's founders to end an ancient war. Hunted by the Guild's enforcers and shadowed by Felix's vengeful sister, Ansel must choose between her oath of silence and the truth that could free the god—and reignite the war he was caged to prevent. In the end she breaks the sigil, releasing the god into a world that has forgotten him, and pays the price: her own memories of everyone she loves, including Felix, who survives her as the only one left to remember her.
about_author: Lior Dravenmoor is a former archivist who claims to have catalogued a manuscript no library will admit owning. They write fantasy from a coastal town where the fog arrives, they insist, exactly on schedule.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She audits the Vellum Guild's ledgers, trading in bottled grief and borrowed years, while privately mourning the silence of her sworn god. A routine audit reveals an entry in her own handwriting she never wrote. Beat: unease beneath routine; the past is already reaching for her.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Weighing Door
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A bleeding stranger, Felix, collapses at the Guild's weighing door clutching a sealed map. He presses it into her hands and dies naming her by a title she's never held: Sigil-Bearer. Beat: shock and unwilling inheritance; the story's engine ignites.

chapters.title: What the Map Refused to Be
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The map resists reading—its ink shifts, and it burns her sigil-scarred palm when she lies about it. She hides it from her Guild superiors, her first true act of treachery. Beat: guilt entwined with curiosity; duty begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Counts the Dead
chapters.summary: Maren's POV (Felix's sister). Maren arrives in the city tracking her brother's killer, certain the Guild is involved. She witnesses Ansel leaving the weighing door with Felix's blood still on the stones. Beat: cold grief sharpening into purpose; the hunter enters the board.

chapters.title: Ledgers Written in a Dead Hand
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She cross-references the map against the Guild's founding ledgers and finds pages excised a century ago—the same year the god went silent. The Guild's First Auditor begins asking gentle, dangerous questions. Beat: dread deepening; the institution she serves is the suspect.

chapters.title: The God Who Did Not Die
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, dream-vision. Her sigil pulls her into a shared dream where a voice—her silent god—speaks for the first time in a hundred years, saying only: 'I was not abandoned. I was buried.' Beat: awe and horror; faith inverted.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Bottling Room
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. To decode the map she trades an impossible thing: three years of her own memory, stored in a Guild vial. The map opens, revealing the god's prison beneath the Guild's oldest vault. Beat: sacrifice as currency; the price of survival becomes literal.

chapters.title: Maren Closes the Distance
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren corners Ansel in a market alley; their fight ends in stalemate when Ansel's sigil flares and Maren recognizes the mark from Felix's letters. She demands the truth instead of blood. Beat: enemies forced into wary alliance; grief meets guilt.

chapters.title: The Founders' Confession
chapters.summary: Shared POV, alternating. Following the map's route, Ansel and Maren find the founders' hidden testament: the Guild didn't serve the god—it imprisoned him to end a war, then built a trade empire on the silence. Beat: the world tilts; every oath Ansel swore was built on a lie.

chapters.title: What Ansel Forgot
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The memory vial's absence begins to hollow her—she can't recall her mother's face, then Felix's dying words. Maren notices Ansel is trading pieces of herself away and names it plainly: 'You're paying for the truth with the person you were.' Beat: tenderness and alarm; love against duty crystallizes.

chapters.title: The First Auditor's Kindness
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The First Auditor reveals she has known about the map all along and offers Ansel a choice: surrender it and be restored, honored, and forgiven—or be declared apostate and hunted. Beat: temptation offered gently; the trap wears a friendly face.

chapters.title: Maren's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren learns Felix wasn't murdered by the Guild—he stole the map to free the god and died carrying it, and the enforcers simply finished what the road began. Her vengeance loses its target and gains a cause. Beat: grief transmuted into conviction.

chapters.title: Apostate
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel refuses the Auditor's bargain. Declared apostate, she flees with Maren as Guild enforcers seal the city gates. Her sigil now burns constantly—the god, or the prison, knows she's coming. Beat: the point of no return; hunted and unburdened at once.

chapters.title: The Undercity of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The fugitives descend through the undercity, where the Guild stores stolen time, and witness what a century of hoarded years has done to the people it was taken from. Beat: horror and compassion; the true cost of the Guild's trade made flesh.

chapters.title: The God's Side of the Story
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, dream-vision. The god shows her the war's end: he agreed to be buried to stop a genocide committed in his name, and the Guild's founders twisted mercy into monopoly. He does not ask to be freed—he asks to be remembered. Beat: moral complexity; freedom may be a second violence.

chapters.title: The Choice Before the Door
chapters.summary: Shared POV. At the vault door, Ansel and Maren argue: Maren wants the god freed for Felix's sake; Ansel fears reigniting the war. Ansel realizes the sigil isn't a lock on the god—it's a lock on the truth, and she is the last key. Beat: love against duty at full tension.

chapters.title: The First Auditor Descends
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The Auditor and enforcers breach the undercity. In the confrontation, the Auditor confesses the Guild has been dying for decades—without the god's silence to trade against, their ledgers are empty. They need Ansel to break the seal so they can own the aftermath. Beat: betrayal revealed; even the villain's motive is desperation.

chapters.title: Sigil-Bearer
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Cornered, wounded, Ansel accepts the title Felix gave her. She understands at last: the god chose a bearer not to free him but to witness him—to carry the truth out even if the prison stands. She presses her sigil to the map and reads it aloud. Beat: acceptance of destiny on her own terms.

chapters.title: The Breaking
chapters.summary: Shared POV, climax. The sigil shatters. The god rises—not as a weapon but as a memory made manifest, flooding the city with the war's true history. The Guild's lies collapse in a single night; the Auditor's empire of silence ends mid-sentence. Beat: cathartic, terrible release; the war does not return, but nothing survives unchanged.

chapters.title: The Price Named Plainly
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Freed, the god comes to Ansel and names the cost of her broken oath: the memories she traded, and the ones her oath held—she will forget everyone she loves. Maren begs her to refuse. Ansel, having spent the book paying in pieces, pays the whole price willingly. Beat: devastating, chosen sacrifice; love against duty resolved in favor of love.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Was Not There
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Ansel wakes with no memory of Felix, Maren, or the god—only the ledgers' habits and an unexplained scar. Maren chooses not to force the past on her but stays near, becoming her friend from scratch. Beat: bittersweet tenderness; grief learning to be gentle.

chapters.title: Felix and the Sigil, Revisited
chapters.summary: Maren's POV, closing. Maren begins writing a book—Felix's story, the god's story, Ansel's story—so that memory, the thing everyone in this tale paid for, is finally kept by choice rather than theft. Ansel, reading the draft, feels something stir. Beat: quiet hope; remembering as an act of love that may, someday, give Ansel back to herself.
